steps.clueRiddle:
An underground train that rolls on rubber tires.
Trace the route before you ride it.
steps.clueReveal: Walk five minutes to Guy-Concordia station. First trace the route on the app map. Then ride it for real to Place-d'Armes.

challenges.title: Metro Navigator
challenges.instructions: Drag your finger along the right lines. Go green to Berri-UQAM, then orange. Stop at Place-d'Armes station.

steps.funFact: Montréal metro trains run on rubber tires, so the ride is very quiet.

steps.clueRiddle:
Blue as the night sky with stars made of gold,
and an organ so loud the whole room shakes.
steps.clueReveal: The station exit is right by the basilica. Go inside at 110 Rue Notre-Dame Ouest. Use quiet voices and find five things.

challenges.title: I-Spy in the Basilica
challenges.instructions: Look up, then look all around you. Find each of the five things. Keep your voice to a whisper.

steps.funFact: The basilica ceiling is deep blue and covered with thousands of gold stars.

steps.clueRiddle:
Cobblestones, jugglers and a painter's chair.
An old square full of fun — find it there.
steps.clueReveal: Walk to Place Jacques-Cartier in Old Montréal. It is a busy cobblestone square. Spot five things while you wander.

challenges.title: Busker Bingo
challenges.instructions: Watch the performers in the square. Find all five things on your list. Clap for anyone who earns it.

steps.funFact: This square is named for Jacques Cartier, the sailor who mapped this river.

steps.clueRiddle:
Down by the old port, nothing says do not touch.
Use your hands and your brain just as much.
steps.clueReveal: Who's got the brains? Walk downhill to 2 Rue de la Commune Ouest. Try the hands-on exhibits, then answer three questions.

challenges.title: Hands-On Three
challenges.instructions: Try any three exhibits from this list. Really play with them, do not just look. Check off the ones you did.
checklist: An exhibit you push or pull
An exhibit with water or air

challenges.title: Science Test
challenges.instructions: Three science questions for the roadblock. Read each one carefully. You can guess if you are stuck.

trivia.q: Which of these is a simple machine?
trivia.funFact: A lever lets a small push move a very heavy thing.

trivia.q: What do we call water when it turns into a gas?
trivia.funFact: Water becomes steam at 100 degrees Celsius.

trivia.q: Which force pulls you back down when you jump?
trivia.funFact: Gravity also keeps the Moon circling around the Earth.

steps.funFact: The Science Centre sits on a pier where real ships used to dock.

steps.clueRiddle:
A crispy tube filled with sweet white cream.
Ask for it in French to live the dream.
steps.clueReveal: Take the metro to Laurier and walk to Café Olimpico. Order your cannoli in French. Then taste it and give your rating.

challenges.title: Order in French
challenges.instructions: Practise the phrase on the card twice. Then say it to the person at the counter. Do not forget to say merci.

challenges.title: Cannoli Judge
challenges.instructions: Take a bite of the cannoli. Think about the crunch and the cream. Give it your maple leaf rating.

steps.funFact: Café Olimpico opened in 1970 and stays open until midnight.

steps.clueRiddle:
One last metro ride and the day is spent.
Back to Mackay Street — leg three is done.
steps.clueReveal: Ride the metro back to Guy-Concordia. Walk to Hôtel Monroe on Rue Mackay. Step onto the pit stop mat.
steps.funFact: You walked through 400 years of Montréal history in a single day.
